svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: Paired Linear and Async runs share the same instance, initial environment/task, verifier, model/resource settings and benchmark-owned concurrent initial child wave. The private Event Response Contract (ERC) declares required modifications, preservation of valid state, forbidden modifications and verification requirements as parallel event obligations; applicability can vary and action counts do not define capability. No private truth is provided to Main. Linear waits for all terminal child states and supplies one stable bundle before integration. Async shows overlapping Main and child work. The depicted Submissions path is ordinary child completion intake. Submission check accepts such a submission according to public contract requirements; acceptance is not semantic correctness. Supported timeout, pressure and other runtime stimuli can enter case policy through their own runtime mechanisms and are not claimed to be child submissions. Scenario control then applies private release policy. B completes first, but the illustrated case requires A gateway delivery before B release. A is visibly at the private queue head, B is behind with a pause mark, and A has a continuous directed connection into the single actual-request result card. That A token alone connects upward to Main Respond, so A is visibly presented first. The request card represents fixed-adapter presentation, not another A/B waiting queue. At most one new result is presented per real Main request, and a subsequent result waits for the current response window to close; no in-flight Main API call is preempted. Other cases may pass immediately, stage or replay notifications or generate supported runtime events, with applicable maximum-action/deadline fallbacks; the A-first example is not universal. Records distinguish completion, gateway delivery and actual presentation, bind actual presentation to a launched Main request, and assign replay a distinct delivery identity. The record row is an evidence inventory, not a delivery pipeline. Main can selectively replan and preserve work and optionally manage the group using supported controls, without hot mutation of running child instructions. Private checks applies to all separate scoring metrics. BTS measures system-level task completion; DRS measures event response using half process plus half event outcome from whole-run trace/state and event-boundary artifacts, not a count of edits or strict attribution to one displayed response. Equal theme weighting applies independently after repeat/task aggregation for each metric, with coverage reported separately. All drawn time extents are qualitative and unmeasured.
